decision: Use explicit {{RUN_ID}} tokens in repeatable Qubes campaign manifests, materialized by the qrexec harness with a validated DIG_CAMPAIGN_RUN_ID or generated UUID, so each qualification run has fresh request-journal and mission idempotency identities while preserving the same protocol and scenario semantics.
problem: The canonical lease-fencing manifest used fixed requestId and submit idempotencyKey values. Re-running it against the same durable coordinator could therefore reuse committed journal responses or the prior mission graph, making nominally independent multi-run qualification evidence depend on cached state instead of fresh execution.

reviewers.preferred: explicit run-scoped request and mission idempotency identities
reviewers.reason: fresh identifiers force each run to exercise durable begin/commit, mission creation, claim, fencing, and QA-join behavior instead of inheriting a prior committed request

reviewers.preferred: validated externally-settable run ID with deterministic token substitution
reviewers.reason: operators can correlate the exact run across qrexec/fault-service configuration without adding a new unauthenticated control channel; unsafe or ambiguous run IDs fail closed

reviewers.preferred: materialize the manifest before transport and leave runQrexecCampaignSteps unchanged
reviewers.reason: adds no qrexec round trips, no daemon, no database, negligible CPU/memory cost, and keeps the tested worker/coordinator protocol unchanged

alternatives.name: keep static request IDs and reset/delete durable stores between runs
alternatives.correctness: can produce fresh runs only if the operator resets every relevant store correctly
alternatives.robustness: weak because manual cleanup can omit the request journal or mission store and destroys useful recovery state

alternatives.name: automatically rewrite every campaign request/idempotency field with an opaque internal suffix
alternatives.robustness: weaker for fault campaigns because external qrexec fault-service configuration may need to know the exact request ID before invocation
alternatives.regressionRisk: medium because hidden rewriting changes manifest semantics and complicates diagnosis

alternatives.name: explicit {{RUN_ID}} token materialization with optional DIG_CAMPAIGN_RUN_ID
alternatives.correctness: fresh request-journal and mission idempotency identities per run while preserving intentionally shared worker IDs for lease-fencing tests
alternatives.robustness: deterministic and inspectable; supports externally coordinated fault-service request IDs and generated UUIDs for ordinary runs
alternatives.resources: linear in manifest size and negligible compared with qrexec execution
alternatives.regressionRisk: low because only pre-transport manifest data changes and lower-level campaign execution remains unchanged

tests: recursive replacement covers requestId, submit idempotencyKey, mutationKey, and nested evidence strings
two distinct run IDs materialize distinct durable identities
the source manifest is not mutated
requireRunToken fails closed for a static manifest when independence is required
unsafe run IDs containing spaces or unsupported characters are rejected
the canonical lease-fencing manifest uses {{RUN_ID}} for every request ID and all durable/idempotency mutation identities
GitHub Node QA and Swift QA must be green on the exact resulting head before using the manifest for Qubes qualification

failuresAndLessons: Unique provenance runId values alone do not make executions independent if the underlying request journal and mission idempotency keys are reused.
Resetting durable stores between qualification runs weakens the very persistence/recovery behavior being qualified and is easy to perform incompletely.
Worker IDs intentionally remain stable in the lease-fencing scenario because same-worker reclaim is the property under test; request and mission identities, not worker identity, must be run-scoped.
This change makes repeated campaigns fresh, but it still does not replace real Qube-to-Qube qrexec evidence or cryptographic/dom0 attestation.
